summary: Klamath County co-op site: a rag camp or compass lookout c.1910, a D-6 cupola cabin in the 1920s, gone by the 1930s (sources differ on the year).

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (1920s) on a site first used c.1910 as a rag camp or compass lookout
facts.status_note: Cupola gone by the 1930s per FFLOS, or 1928 per firelookout.com; the Klamath County blog says it may have moved to Chase Mountain; no source describes remains
facts.agency: Klamath Forest Protective Association co-op, Crater National Forest

events.note: Rag camp on the site (FFLOS); camp (firelookout.com); compass lookout c.1910 (Klamath County blog)
1910 association report places a patrolman at his lookout on Aspen Mountain when fires started (Oregon Lookouts page reprint); the report may not name this summit
Foster 1916 report: station maintained as a cooperative station with the Klamath Patrol Association
Newspaper item names E.P. Miller as a lookout in the forestry service at Mt. Aspen
D-6 cupola constructed; FFLOS gives the 1920's, firelookout.com 1920s (decade only, 1920 is a placeholder)
FFLOS: gone sometime in the 1930's (no exact year given)
Believed (not confirmed) that the cupola was moved to Chase Mountain for living quarters in the early 1930s; year is approximate
Coast and Geodetic Survey station recovered; bronze tablet in bedrock at the highest point, marks in good condition; directions given
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register November 15, 2019 (US 1819, OR 542)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the cupola was gone sometime in the 1930s; firelookout.com says gone in 1928. The story reports both and does not choose.
FFLOS and firelookout.com both say the cupola is gone; the Klamath County blog says it may have been moved to Chase Mountain, presented as a belief. The story reports the blog's claim as unconfirmed.

sources.title: Aspen Butte Lookout (page headed McCartie Ranch Fire Lookout Tower)

notes_for_editor: The firelookout.com page is headed 'McCartie Ranch Fire Lookout Tower' above the Aspen Butte entry, and gives 18 miles WNW of Klamath Falls where the 1933 survey note says 18 miles W; the title mismatch suggests a copied header, so it is cited only for the 1910 camp, the 1920s cupola and the 1928 date. Township differs: weebly gives 37S-6E-35, the blog gives Sec 26 T37S R6E; not used in the story. The 1910 and 1915 items on the Oregon Lookouts page mention 'Aspen Mountain' and 'Aspen Lake mountain', which may be different summits, so the story hedges the 1910 patrolman. A Chase Mountain lookout page (NHLR) describes a 1951 metal tower and another (cherylhill.net) says a 1920s tower and 1928 ground cabin stood there; neither excerpt mentions an Aspen cupola, so the Chase Mountain move is unconfirmed. The 1933 Coast and Geodetic Survey directions are omitted as too old to be useful for access. No newspaper archive or Forest Service document was consulted.
